metaDescription: Digital marketing for Minneapolis businesses: SEO, paid ads, social media, websites and video, planned by neighbourhood, suburb and season.
lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) is a digital marketing agency that works remotely with Minneapolis businesses on SEO, paid advertising, social media, websites and video. Minneapolis is a headquarters city with strong neighbourhoods, a twin across the river and a winter that changes how people shop for months at a time. We build marketing around the part of the metro you serve and the season your customers are in.

sections.heading: A corporate city with a neighbourhood economy
paragraphs: Minneapolis grew up on flour milling at the falls of the Mississippi, and it still punches above its size as a business centre. A major national retailer and a large bank have their headquarters downtown, big food, healthcare and medical device companies sit in the surrounding suburbs, and the University of Minnesota brings students, research and hospital staff. Around these employers is a dense layer of law firms, consultancies, design studios and software companies that sell to them.

The other Minneapolis is local. The North Loop's old warehouses hold restaurants, boutiques and offices. Northeast is known for artists' studios and breweries. Uptown and the streets around the Chain of Lakes mix apartments, shops and fitness studios, and areas such as Linden Hills and Longfellow have their own small commercial corners. An independent restaurant in Northeast and a business software firm downtown need completely different plans, even though they share a postcode range.

sections.heading: Minneapolis, St. Paul and the suburbs are separate searches
paragraphs: People in the metro think of Minneapolis and St. Paul as two cities, and they search that way. Someone in St. Paul's Highland Park looks for a dentist in St. Paul, not across the river. The suburbs behave the same: Edina, St. Louis Park, Bloomington, Plymouth and Minnetonka are all named in searches, and each has its own competitors in the map results.
For a business with one location, this means deciding honestly how far customers will travel, then building visibility for that area first.
bullets: Pages for the neighbourhoods and suburbs you really serve, written with local detail and not just a changed place name.
A Google Business Profile with accurate categories, hours and service area.
A simple routine for asking customers for reviews.
Ad targeting by distance, with separate budgets where the west suburbs and the city perform differently.
Call and form tracking, so you know which channel brought the customer.

sections.heading: Marketing through a Minneapolis winter
paragraphs: Cold weather moves life indoors. Downtown workers use the skyways, deliveries rise, and gyms, restaurants and entertainment venues compete for people who would rather stay home. Heating companies, snow removal crews and auto shops face sudden demand after a storm or a deep freeze, and the firms that have ads and pages ready in advance take the calls.

Then the city turns outward. Patios open, the lakes and trails fill, festivals and farmers' markets return, and home improvement, landscaping and real estate hit their busy months. In late summer the State Fair draws much of the region for nearly two weeks. We plan content and budgets around these shifts with you.

sections.heading: Selling to the companies headquartered here
paragraphs: Many Minneapolis firms sell services to large corporate buyers. Those buyers compare suppliers quietly online before any meeting. A website that explains what you do in plain terms, shows the kind of work you take on and answers the questions a procurement team asks will do more than a general brand campaign. We pair that with search content for specific problems and LinkedIn campaigns aimed at the right roles.

cards.heading: Who we can help in Minneapolis

items.title: Restaurants, breweries and cafes
items.text: Short video, strong photography and active map listings bring people in, especially when winter keeps them home.

items.title: Professional and business services
items.text: Law, accounting, consulting and design firms win work with a clear page for each service and search visibility for specific needs.

items.title: Health and medical technology
items.text: Clinics and device suppliers need accurate, careful content and ad wording that respects platform rules on health claims.

items.title: Home services and contractors
items.text: Heating, roofing, remodelling and snow work are searched by suburb. Area pages and call ads capture that demand.

items.title: Retail and consumer brands
items.text: Shops and brands selling online need stores that load fast, product photography and ads measured against margin.

items.title: Software and technology firms
items.text: Product companies need search content, paid acquisition and a site that turns visits into demos or trials.

presence: TDM works with Minneapolis businesses remotely. We do not have an office or a team member in the city. Work is delivered online by our team, with scheduled video calls and written reports.

faqs.a: No. We work with Minneapolis businesses remotely. You deal with our team through video calls, shared documents and regular reports.

faqs.q: Do I need separate marketing for Minneapolis and St. Paul?
faqs.a: If you want customers in both, yes in practice. People search by their own city and suburb, so you need pages, reviews and ad targeting for each area you serve.

faqs.q: How should a Minneapolis business advertise in winter?
faqs.a: Match the offer to how people live in the cold: delivery, indoor experiences, urgent heating and snow services. Have storm-related ads ready beforehand and move budget back toward outdoor and home projects as spring arrives.

faqs.q: How much does digital marketing cost in Minneapolis?
faqs.a: Pricing depends on the scope of work. We discuss your goals in a free consultation and then send a quote.

faqs.q: How long before a new website or campaign is live?
faqs.a: That depends on your requirements and the brief. We agree the timeline in the plan before work starts.
